transcript.text: In this video, you’ll design a still title: type on it, move it around, and style it.
Switch to Still. The interface turns pink, and the player goes away: this title is an image.
Double-click a title to type on it directly. Everything updates live.
Select letters to style just those. Here, Control Shift and the greater-than key make them bigger.
Or recolour them in the Colour section of the inspector.
Press Escape when you’re done typing.
Drag a title to move it anywhere on the artboard.
Drag a corner handle to scale it.
Drag the round handle above it to rotate. Hold Shift to snap to fifteen degrees.
Control Z undoes the last change.
With the title selected, the arrow keys nudge it one pixel at a time, or ten with Shift.
The Effects tab adds strokes, shadows, glows, bevels and 3D. Start from a ready-made style.
Then fine-tune each effect in the list below. The top of the list is drawn on top.
Warp bends the whole title, like Photoshop’s Warp Text, or sets the letters along a curve.
To add another title, press T, click the artboard, and type.
Every title is a layer. Show or hide it, lock it, or drag to reorder.
Your work is saved in this browser by itself. Save title makes a file to back it up, or open on another computer, with its fonts inside.
